title: Ops Runway: compact orchestration checklist + annotated notes (Sept 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, day-of-release orchestration checklist and annotated notes file intended for small-to-medium releases where we want a single-page actionable runway plus a draft of release notes. Use this for feature rollouts that require a controlled cutover window (1-3 hours).

High-level objectives:
- Minimize blast radius with staged traffic routing and brief canary period.
- Validate critical KPIs (latency, error-rate, throughput) within 20 minutes post-cutover.
- Clear fallback/rollback path and owner responsibilities.

Preflight (T-48h to T-1h):
- T-48h: Finalize merge window and tag release candidate. Owner: release lead (Ethan Brooks).
- T-24h: Confirm infra capacity reservation (Dedicated pool + burst) and region allocation. Owner: Mateo Alvarez.
- T-12h: Run full integration smoke suite against staging (green required). Test id: RR-SMOKE-0915.
- T-6h: Lock feature flags for rollout; create canary route config in console.
- T-2h: Notify #release-ops and customer-success stakeholders with timeline and expected impact. Include link to live health dashboard.
- T-1h: Snapshot telem dashboards, create short-lived dashboard link, stash baseline perf metrics.

Cutover day timeline (example window: 02:00–04:00 UTC):
- 02:00 UTC — Preflight signoff (owners: QA, SRE, Product). Checklist tick.
- 02:10 UTC — Deploy RC to canary subset (5% traffic).
- 02:12–02:25 UTC — Canary validation window (monitor 1xx/4xx/5xx, 95 Pctl latency).
- 02:25 UTC — If canary OK, advance to progressive rollout (25% -> 60% -> 100%) with 10–15m holds between steps.
- 03:30 UTC — Post-100% validation, announce GA to internal channels and toggle feature flags where necessary.
- 04:00 UTC — Begin post-deploy monitoring cadence (see post-deploy).

Cutover guardrails and thresholds (immediate abort if any met):
- Error-rate (5xx) > 1.5x baseline for 5 minutes.
- User-visible latency (95th) increases > 2x baseline or absolute > 600ms for 5 minutes.
- Token throughput drops more than 20% vs expected capacity for sustained 10 minutes.
- Any customer-facing severity-1 reported within canary window.

Quick rollback recipe (3-step fallback):
1) Pause progressive rollout in console and revert traffic to previous model variant or previous stack snapshot (blue). Owner: release lead.
2) If rollback fails or symptoms persist, cut traffic to safety tier (read-only mode / degraded mode) using safety-lane. Owner: SRE on-call.
3) Open incident in PagerDuty, notify exec channel, and start postmortem template (link in linked_artifacts).

Essential smoke tests (run after each rollout step):
- API health: curl -s -I https://api.redwood.ai/health | grep 200
- Generate sample: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hello world","max_tokens":8}' | jq .status
- KV cache sanity: run kv-check script on node (scripts/kv_check.sh) -> expect OK
- Auth + rate-limit: run token-limited request burst script and ensure no auth regressions and 429s as baseline.

Prometheus/Datadog queries (examples):
- 5xx rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (job)
- 95p latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Inflight tokens: sum(gauge_inflight_tokens) by (region)
Put these into the short-lived dashboard link before cutover.

Communication matrix:
- Primary channel: #release-ops (Slack).
- Escalation: PagerDuty (SRE on-call) -> Release lead -> Eng manager -> CTO.
- Customer notices: Customer Success draft (Priya Kapoor) to be ready at T+30m.

Operations checklist (day-of quick ticks):
- [ ] Confirm baseline dashboards and save snapshot link (done at T-1h).
- [ ] Announce go/no-go call at T-55m.
- [ ] Deploy RC to canary (5%).
- [ ] Green/abort decision for canary.
- [ ] Progressive releases: 25% -> 60% -> 100% (holds observed).
- [ ] Run smoke test suite after each stage.
- [ ] Confirm data plane metrics (latency, errors, token throughput).
- [ ] Confirm cost telemetry not spiking anomalously.
- [ ] Finalize internal release notes and customer-facing blurb.

Post-deploy (T+0 to T+72h):
- T+0–T+1h: High cadence monitoring (5m checks). If rollback triggered, proceed with incident runbook.
- T+1–T+24h: Reduced cadence (15m checks) and collect sampling traces for 24h.
- T+24–T+72h: Stability review and metric regression check; schedule rollback window if necessary.

Release notes draft (internal -> customer-ready):
TITLE: "Sept 2026: progressive rollout — performance and reliability updates"
Short summary (internal):
- Rolling out runtime optimizations that improve tail latency and introduce an updated model variant for mid-length prompts. Expect smoother scaling behavior in multi-tenant pools.
Notable changes for customers:
- Improved 95th percentile latency on text-generation for prompts between 64–512 tokens (typical improvement ~15–25%).
- New model flag: model_variant=v2-compact (opt-in; will be default for new Dedicated pools).
- Minor API behaviour: /v1/generate now returns additional field "engine_info" with model variant metadata (non-breaking).
Migration notes and action items for integrators:
- If you pin by model name, please confirm compatibility with v2-compact; full migration guide in Confluence link.
- If you use strict latency SLAs, test on staging: approx 10–15% variation expected during initial week.
Known issues (tracked):
- Memory pressure observed on some 48GB instances under synthetic bursts (mitigation: autoscaler tune recommended). Tracked in RR-1450.
- Intermittent prompt truncation for very long single-token tokens (edge case).

Post-release checklist for docs/CS/sales:
- [ ] Customer-facing release notes finalized and published by T+2h (owner: Priya Kapoor).
- [ ] CS FAQ updated with rollback guidance and expected behaviour.
- [ ] Post-release debrief scheduled (T+3 days) with stakeholders: Product, SRE, Release Eng.

Appendix: quick commands and references
- View rollout config: console.redwood.ai/releases/<release-id>/progress
- Revert traffic: console.redwood.ai/releases/<release-id>/rollback (button + confirmation)
- Trigger smoke locally: ./scripts/run_smoke_local.sh --profile rc-2026-09
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/incident-template

Notes & open questions (for follow-up):
- Should we add a non-disruptive canary traffic mirror to validate cache-warmup separate from production routing? (action: SRE to prototype).
- Add a short automated post-deploy checklist that posts status to #release-ops (action: Developer Experience).

Owners & contact info:
- Release lead: Ethan Brooks (e.brooks@redwood.ai)
- SRE: Mateo Alvarez (m.alvarez@redwood.ai)
- QA: Ava Chen (a.chen@redwood.ai)
- Customer Success: Priya Kapoor (p.kapoor@redwood.ai)

Revision history:
- 2026-09-15 created by Ethan Brooks (initial compact checklist)
- 2026-09-20 updated by Ava Chen (smoke tests added)

End of document.
